hlni.insight: A short illustrative task reveals where you need help or want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
hlni.audienceGap: Students think B.Com and BBA are mutually exclusive paths that require a 'natural' fit.
hlni.viewerChange: Moves from abstract anxiety to identifying a specific skill-based investigation.
hlni.support: The method uses a task to isolate logic constraints versus context, which provides a data point for future course investigation.
hlni.payoff: The student identifies their specific struggle and forms a targeted question, turning a vague choice into a productive inquiry.

candidate.reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: A Practical Comparison
candidate.creativeAngle: Using a task-based journal to shift from anxiety to investigation
candidate.objective: Help students move past the B.Com vs BBA label trap by using a concrete task to identify their actual interests.
candidate.targetAudience: +2 students seeking accessible, supportive guidance, including students worried about marks, confidence, or belonging

shots.name: The Confusion
shots.visual: Two students sitting at a cafe with a notebook, looking stressed.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA feels like guessing your future. Let's stop guessing.

shots.name: The Task
shots.visual: A notebook shows: Example: Problem: Assign 3 shifts to 3 staff.
shots.dialogue: Try this: 'Example: Problem: Assign 3 shifts to 3 staff.' See where you get stuck.
shots.onscreenText: Example: Problem: Assign 3 shifts to 3 staff.
shots.cameraPerformance: Handheld, focus on the notebook entry.

shots.name: The Shift
shots.visual: Student writes in the journal. They look relieved.
shots.dialogue: I struggled with the logic constraints, not the business context. Now I ask: 'Where can I find more practice on logic-based scheduling tasks?'
shots.onscreenText: Where can I find more practice on logic-based scheduling tasks?

productionNotes.camera: Close-ups on the notebook and expressions.
productionNotes.sound: Subtle cafe ambience, soft acoustic background.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Instead of guessing degree suitability, use a specific task to record a 'sticking point' that leads to a concrete question.

selected.title: The Sticking Point Journal
selected.audienceGap: Students feel anxious because they don't know if they are 'naturally' B.Com or BBA material.
selected.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
selected.viewerChange: Moves from self-doubt to identifying concrete areas for investigation.
selected.concept: Two students talk about a sample scheduling task, identifying where they actually got stuck.
selected.device: Natural, informal conversation between two peers using a shared notebook.
selected.support: The observation belongs to this activity and participant; it supports a next question rather than a general prediction.
methodSteps: Try or inspect a clearly illustrative task.
Record one point where you needed help and one question you want to investigate.
Turn the observation into a question for a real course brief or course team.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.visibleProof: A person records a specific sticking point and asks a different, more useful question afterward.
selected.payoff: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.limitations: A brief exercise does not measure aptitude, learning style, long-term interest or academic performance.

demonstration.input: A simple scheduling puzzle for 3 staff members.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Problem: Assign 3 shifts to 3 staff.
demonstration.observation: The student records that they struggled with the logic of the constraints, not the business context.
demonstration.nextQuestion: Where can I find more practice on logic-based scheduling tasks?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: Split-screen comparison of a blank worksheet being filled out while narrating the need for specific criteria.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: Natural, informal conversation between two peers using a shared notebook.

comparedWith.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
comparedWith.device: A quick-fire quiz where the 'correct' answer is that there isn't enough info.

conceptSelection.contrast: Pre-story comparison selected different grounded insights and mechanisms: Trust = assessment_questions / tripartite_question_mapping; Connection = task_question_journal / recorded_sticking_point; Discovery = insufficient_information / forced_choice_refutation. Each has an illustrative input, observable result and next question. This is not editorial approval.
